lesson.grammar_point: social-professional register and discourse management -- opening, holding, redirecting and closing an unscripted conversation (no new structure)

listenings.text: Leonardo, it is Claudia. You land on Sunday, so let me tell you how that conference actually works, because nobody tells you and I wasted two of them finding out. The sessions are not where anything happens. Nothing happens in the sessions. Everything happens in the twenty minutes between them, at the coffee tables, and at the reception on the first evening, which you will want to skip because you will be tired. Do not skip it. Second thing. You will feel that you have to be interesting. You do not. You have to be curious. The most successful person I have ever watched at one of those events asked questions for forty minutes and gave one answer, and three firms called him afterwards. Ask what brought them there. Ask what is keeping them busy this year. And third, the part that people get wrong. Do not try to speak to everybody. Four real conversations beat forty business cards, every time. Get the four, write one line about each of them on your phone the same night, and email them on the Tuesday. Not two weeks later. Tuesday.

I run a professional network for lawyers in about thirty countries, and I want to correct the most common idea I hear about networking, which is that it is a performance. It is not. Nobody at a conference is judging your English. They are wondering whether you are worth twenty more minutes of their afternoon, and that is a completely different test. Here is what actually decides it. First, you have to be able to say what you do in two sentences, and the second sentence has to be the interesting one. Anybody can say I am a tax lawyer. Very few can add the line that makes a stranger lean in, something like, and this year almost all of it has been foreign payment platforms trying to work out what our reform does to them. That is the sentence that starts a conversation. Second, listen for the overlap. Somewhere in the first minute they will mention a problem that touches yours, and that is your opening. And third, the part that nearly everybody skips. The conversation is not the point. The follow-up is the point. A conversation with no follow-up is a nice afternoon. A short email on the Tuesday, with one line about what you discussed, is a relationship. The people who are good at this are not more charming than you. They are just better at Tuesday.

extra_audio.text: I do not think we have met. I am Leonardo Constantino, a partner at ALMA in Sao Paulo. Actually, we advise financial institutions on exactly that, so it has been a busy year for us. Speaking of which, we have been seeing a lot of that with payment platforms coming into Brazil. I would love to continue this conversation. Would you be open to a quick call next week? Let me give you my details, and I will send you a short note on Tuesday.
